readings.core_relation: After each revealed response, coverage-error feedback lowers alpha_t after misses and raises it after coverage, adjusting set inclusion. Summing updates expresses average miscoverage error as a bounded endpoint difference divided by gamma T, explaining long-run target convergence without modeling distribution shifts.
readings.scope: Positive step size and full/empty quantile extensions bound parameter motion. The guarantee concerns accumulated errors, permits extreme sets, and does not ensure short-window coverage.
readings.witness: bounded parameter motion, rather than a correct model

readings.core_relation: Coverage-error feedback adjusts the quantile toward larger sets after misses and smaller sets after coverage, restoring long-run empirical miscoverage to its target under distribution shifts without distributional assumptions.
readings.scope: Requires next-update response availability and full/empty sets. Stronger bounds assume stationary hidden Markov initialization and fixed fitted functions. Time-point coverage is not guaranteed; empirical local improvements depend on score design, and step size trades responsiveness for instability.
readings.witness: This controls accumulated errors, not coverage at every time point.
readings.unclear: Additional regularity conditions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Normalized-score adaptation tracked 90% local coverage better than fixed calibration in selected volatility failures; adaptation also avoided fixed-calibration troughs in ordered county predictions. Unnormalized errors caused wider swings, showing that feedback alone did not stabilize coverage.
readings.scope: Step size 0.005; rolling 1,250-day histories; 500-day stock and 300-county windows. Four panels selected from twelve stocks illustrate failures, not general superiority. County ordering was constructed by time zone and randomized within zones, not actual reporting.
readings.witness: feedback alone therefore did not stabilize local coverage

readings.core_relation: Hierarchical predictions achieved near-target distance loss while remaining mostly leaves, so control did not merely reflect coarse predictions. Segmentation and multilabel losses were near target. Non-monotone losses can break control; a supremum envelope restores it, potentially conservatively.
readings.scope: ImageNet mean 0.0499 at alpha 0.05; segmentation/COCO means 0.0987/0.0996 at alpha 0.1 over 1,000 splits each. Results concern average risk, not every split or wholly correct sets. Different calibration sizes prevent isolating dispersion causes.
readings.witness: predictions are almost always leaf nodes

readings.core_relation: After observing each response, update alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+gamma(alpha-err_t). Misses raise the requested quantile, enlarging sets with fixed scoring functions. Summing updates makes average miscoverage minus alpha equal (alpha_1-alpha_{T+1})/(gamma T), yielding a vanishing frequency discrepancy through bounded feedback.
readings.scope: Requires gamma>0, alpha_1 in [0,1], and full/empty endpoint conventions, which bound alpha_t without clipping. Applies irrespective of the data sequence; controls accumulated errors, not marginal coverage at every time.
readings.witness: The guarantee follows from bounded feedback, not a distributional model

readings.core_relation: Conformal risk control extends binary coverage to error severity by reserving worst-case unseen loss B in calibration, guaranteeing expected test loss at most alpha. Monotonicity connects this conservative choice to a symmetric threshold; boundedness alone cannot ensure control.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeable, bounded, non-increasing, right-continuous losses and a safe endpoint. A sharp lower bound alpha-2B/(n+1) additionally requires i.i.d., nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps. Guarantees average over calibration/test randomness; applications show near-target means over 1,000 splits.
readings.unclear: Specified shift conditions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Choose the infimum lambda satisfying [n R_n(lambda)+B]/(n+1)<=alpha, or a safe maximal parameter. Reserving B dominates the unseen loss; comparison with a symmetric full-sample threshold and monotonicity makes the implementable choice no riskier, enabling expected-risk control without the test outcome.
readings.scope: Requires an upper loss bound, non-increasing losses, exchangeability and right-continuity. The guarantee averages over both calibration and test randomness rather than treating the calibration mean as test risk.
readings.witness: without requiring the test outcome during calibration

readings.core_relation: Corrected calibration yielded near-target false-negative risk rather than substantial undershooting: segmentation averaged 0.0987 and COCO 0.0996 at alpha 0.1. Non-monotone losses can instead approach B, explaining why monotonicity matters.
readings.scope: Across 1,000 splits, standard deviations were 0.0114/0.0052; calibration/evaluation counts were 1,000/781 and 4,000/1,000. Different tasks and calibration sizes prevent isolating dispersion causes. Expected-risk control averages over calibration/test data, not every split or image; findings support the tested monotone losses.
readings.witness: rather than constraining every split or image

readings.core_relation: Normalized-score adaptation kept local volatility coverage nearer 90% than fixed calibration, including a crisis undercoverage case. Unnormalized residuals caused much larger swings despite adaptation, showing that feedback did not compensate for this score choice.
readings.scope: Both refit GARCH on 1,250 days; step size 0.005 and 500-day windows. Four stocks selected from twelve expose fixed-calibration failures, not average advantage. Larger steps partly mitigate swings but increase parameter volatility. Local improvement is empirical, distinct from long-run frequency control.
readings.witness: coverage feedback alone did not compensate for this score choice

readings.core_relation: Worst-case unseen-loss correction extends calibration from binary coverage to expected error severity, guaranteeing loss at most alpha. Monotonicity links selected parameters to control; an upper envelope repairs non-monotone losses but can be conservative.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeable, non-increasing, right-continuous losses bounded by B and a safe endpoint. The sharp lower bound alpha-2B/(n+1) additionally requires i.i.d., nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps. Control averages calibration/test randomness, not every fitted set; non-monotone risk can approach B. Four application types use 1,000 splits.
readings.witness: rather than certifying risk for every fitted set

readings.core_relation: Reserving worst-case unseen loss in calibration controls expected graded error at alpha, beyond binary coverage. Non-monotone losses can approach B despite a lower target; monotone upper envelopes restore control with possible conservatism.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeable, bounded, non-increasing, right-continuous losses with safe terminal losses. A tight 2B/(n+1) undershoot bound additionally requires i.i.d., nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps. Four applications show near-target means over 1,000 splits; shift extensions need specified weighting information.
readings.witness: making the loss's dependence on the prediction parameter central
readings.unclear: Required shift weighting information is not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Coverage-error feedback updates alpha_t after each response: misses lower it and request wider sets. Quantile extensions bound its movement, so summing updates gives average(err_t)-alpha=(alpha_1-alpha_{T+1})/(gamma T), controlling accumulated errors without estimating distribution shifts.
readings.scope: Requires gamma>0, alpha_1 in [0,1], and non-decreasing quantiles extended to full/empty sets. Stronger marginal-error analysis assumes stationary hidden Markov initialization, fixed score/quantile functions, Lipschitz statewise miscoverage, and an interior target-attaining parameter in every state.

readings.core_relation: Choose the smallest lambda satisfying [n R_n(lambda)+B]/(n+1)<=alpha, falling back to a safe maximum. Reserving B for unseen loss makes this choice at least as large as a full-sample oracle's; non-increasing losses make it no riskier, establishing finite-sample expected-risk control.
readings.scope: Requires a common upper loss bound and a maximal parameter whose loss is at most alpha. Exchangeability links oracle test loss to its full average; right-continuity ensures threshold attainment.
readings.witness: The correction reserves room for an unseen loss as large as B

readings.core_relation: Coverage-error feedback requests wider sets after misses and narrower sets after coverage, restoring target long-run miscoverage despite distribution shifts. Stock and constructed county experiments show local improvements; score normalization remains consequential.
readings.scope: Requires immediate feedback and endpoint extensions; not time-point coverage. Stronger bounds assume stationary hidden Markov initialization and fixed score/quantile functions, relating error to target-attaining parameter changes. Larger steps trade responsiveness for volatility; weaker adaptation approaches fixed calibration.
readings.witness: Coverage feedback therefore complements score design rather than replacing it.
readings.unclear: Additional regularity conditions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Segmentation and COCO achieved near-target average false-negative risk, with greater split variation in segmentation. This supports expected-risk control, not splitwise caps. Non-monotone losses can approach B; an upper envelope restores control with possible conservatism.
readings.scope: At alpha 0.1 over 1,000 splits, means/standard deviations were 0.0987/0.0114 and 0.0996/0.0052; calibration/evaluation sizes were 1,000/781 and 4,000/1,000. Different tasks/models prevent attributing COCO's smaller spread solely to calibration size. Monotone examples do not establish control for arbitrary bounded losses.
readings.witness: the theorem does not cap risk separately for every split

readings.core_relation: Adaptation improved local coverage beyond shared rolling refitting: normalized volatility coverage stayed near 90%, and county coverage avoided fixed-calibration troughs. Removing volatility normalization worsened swings despite feedback, qualifying the improvement.
readings.scope: Both use 1,250-day histories; gamma 0.005; 500-day stock/300-county windows. Four displayed stocks were selected failures among twelve, with favorable adaptation reported for all twelve. Counties were time-zone ordered and randomized within zones, not actual reporting order. Local gains are empirical, not implied by long-run frequency control.
readings.witness: not consequences of the unrestricted long-run frequency guarantee

readings.core_relation: Choose the smallest lambda satisfying (n R_n(lambda)+B)/(n+1)<=alpha, or a safe maximum. The B correction upper-bounds the full calibration-plus-test average; comparison with its oracle and non-increasing losses ensures no larger test loss, converting calibration into finite-sample expected-risk control.
readings.scope: Requires a common upper bound and maximal-parameter loss at most alpha. Exchangeability makes the held-out test function representative conditional on the unordered collection; right-continuity ensures oracle constraint attainment.
readings.witness: this comparison converts an empirical calibration rule into a finite-sample expected-risk guarantee

readings.core_relation: Outcome feedback adjusts quantile levels, increasing after misses and decreasing after coverage, guaranteeing target realized miscoverage frequency despite drift. Volatility and county examples show better local coverage than fixed calibration; normalization still matters.
readings.scope: Requires each response, fixed positive step size, and full/empty sets; not time-point coverage. Stronger bounds assume stationary hidden Markov structure and fixed score/quantile functions, linking error to environmental dependence and optimal-parameter changes. Removing normalization widens swings despite feedback.
readings.witness: Feedback therefore complements score design rather than replacing it
readings.unclear: Additional regularity conditions are not recoverable.
